reviews.text: I've had the pleasure of doing some early playtesting pre-release on Wunder, accidently sunk a bit more time into it than I planned! I love games where I get to strategize broken combinations, and I get the same kick in this as I do in games like Balatro, but there's a bit of a twist here! Since the coins have two sides, it's not all about just trying to score the highest amount possible - going all in with one powerful coin might not work out if it lands on the wrong side! It's a balancing act of both making sure you make your coins powerful and reliable enough to beat the goal - when you get the choice to upgrade your coin to make it twice as powerful, or 10% more likely to land on heads... which do you pick?? Is your 70% heads chance enough to make your critical combo land with a couple of chances, or will chasing higher score lead to your loss? The game is great fun if you're into this kind of thing, looks & sounds good, has a good amount of variety, and dev has been making loads of improvements up to release, so hopefully that continues throughout early access! there's already a load of content here but I can't wait to see what's next! Plus I still have a bunch left to unlock!

I already played the demo before and loved it and now with the early access release it is still a lot of fun and I'm excited to see which improvements will come, which new features will be added and so on! If you like quota games WUNDER is a really unique and fun one! Oh and the best part if you are deep into a run and need to leave, no worries you can just quit the run and continue later :)
Really fun game with a cool twist on the standard deckbuilders. The constant state of chance of coin flips keeps it interesting every round! Addictive as hell!!

Wunder: The Double-Sided Deckbuilder is a really creative take on the roguelike deckbuilder genre. The coin flipping mechanics make every run feel different, especially once you start combining abilities and charms together to create strong synergies. It’s one of those games where you keep thinking ‘just one more run’ because there’s always another way you could have played it or decision you could have made. I also really like the overall theme and atmosphere. Travelling through the underworld along the River Styx gives the game a unique identity, and the world already feels interesting. It genuinely feels like it has the potential to become a really deep and memorable world as it gets fleshed out more over time, but there’s already more than enough content and variety to stay engaged and have fun with right now. The visuals, music, and gameplay all work well together, and the mix of strategy, charm synergies, and unpredictable coin flips keeps the runs exciting from start to finish. If you enjoy deckbuilders or roguelike games, this is definitely worth checking out

I've really enjoyed playing this, its a really good twist on deckbuilders. I'm looking forward to seeing the development of this game as more things get added and improved. Definitely a game to play and keep an eye on.

I rarely ever play deck builders but thought I would give this one a try Really fun game with a great twist to the usual style of deck builders, the coin flips keep it really interesting! Very addictive and excited to see what future updates the game will get!
Really fun, solid deck builder. Wasn't sure what to expect but I haven't been able to stop playing since buying it, highly recommend!

This game has awesome balance and depth for an early access game about flipping coins! It's really compelling. I like that it's a bit deceptive, everyone understands heads or tails, the game doesn't ask you to learn special hands or anything complex at all off the bat.. But in each run you find new items or rare coins that you really want to try and build around! I've played for a few hours on steamdeck, just using the touchscreen/ cursor, and you can see a little bit of UI overlap in places outside of the main gameplay, but it's perfectly playable. There's loads of challenge here too, I have only made it to river 3 so far just playing casually and my run normally ends before then.. I've seen on discord there's at least 8 levels and the scores can get silly big. It's a really well conceived game, easily worth twice the price I paid for it during deck builder fest.

If you're a fan of deckbuilders, but want to try something slightly different in the genre, definitely give this a try! Has all the usual shenanigans and chaos of regular deckbuilders but with fun coin flip mechanics that are super satisfying and a change of pace to the usual formula. Absolutely loved giving this a play and will continue following it through EA
Lovely cheap little deckbuilder with a twist; flipping coins :D Great progression and tons of potential by an active developer with regular game updates!
Game good.

I’ll admit out of the gate that I’m not usually the biggest fan of deckbuilders. That said, a few games manage to break through that bias, and so far, Wunder has absolutely proven itself to be one of them. The premise is simple: flip coins and see how far they can take you. Beneath that simplicity, however, is an incredible amount of depth. With just under two hours of playtime at the time of writing, I’m already thinking about potential builds for future runs, which I think alone speaks to the quality of the experience. That’s not even mentioning the presentation, which is top-notch across the board. Given my general feelings toward the genre, I’m not sure how much long-term mileage I’ll personally get out of Wunder. Still, for anyone already invested in deckbuilders and looking for a fresh game to really sink their teeth into, this is an easy recommendation. Especially at its current price point.
A suprisingly good timewaster. Good concept and plays well.

Game has a simple gameplay loop with very cool complexities to explore, my first run I was proud of my coin giving me like 100 value and then on my second run i was able to make a single coin give 100,000. Reminds me of the fun parts of balatro, as somebody who loves deck builders and roguelikes this one has been a great addition, excited to see it grow in early access.

Really enjoyed my first trips down the river! Took just a few minutes to grasp the basics and before I knew it, an hour had zoomed by. Not my typical game choice, but really glad I gave it a shot. The mechanics are fun and you can tell the developer really put some love into it: the art and sound effects are equally clever and pleasing. Give Wunder a try!
this has a lot of potential and i like how elegant it looks and feels!
This is Damn fun! I watched A youtuber play this game, and bought it within 30 seconds. This type of game just speaks to me. Looking forward to more updates!

Very fun game to play, always having to build your deck around the possibility of the coin landing on either side brings more depth to the game. There are many fun combos and loops to explore especially with imbuing the coin with different elements and being able to manipulate the coins to fit your deck. would recommend
This one is very promising. I really enjoyed it but it needs controller support, would be great on Steam Deck if it had.

5th run in and I managed to use the hyda coin to go endless and get 10^10 points. Really cool roguelike, love the concept of having coins instead of cards that have different effects depending on whether you land heads or tails.
